facts.raw_span: no specific ocular symptoms
no history of eye surgery
lipid and glucose levels within normal range
Best spectacle-corrected visual acuity: 20/20 OU
Normal conjunctiva with healthy ocular adnexa
4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma
Ring characteristics: Complete rings, outermost ring ~4mm from limbus
Ring measurements (vertical diameters from periphery to center): 6.0mm, 4.8mm, 4.5mm, and 3.6mm
Surface of rings: smooth without obvious deposits, pigmentation, or serrations
Normal corneal sensations bilaterally
Keratometry readings: 43.4 × 43.4 D OD and 43.0 × 44.8 D OS
Serum copper levels: Normal

concepts.why: The presence of 4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma with smooth surfaces and no obvious deposits or pigmentation is consistent with Corneal Arcus.
The combination of normal corneal sensations, keratometry readings, and the presence of ring-shaped opacities in the posterior corneal stroma is suggestive of Fuchs' Endothelial Dystrophy.
The presence of posterior crocodile shagreen in conjunction with ring-shaped opacities is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of a small nasal pterygium is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of mild nuclear sclerosis of the crystalline lens is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of ring-shaped opacities in the posterior corneal stroma is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of normal corneal sensations and healthy ocular adnexa is not consistent with Dry Eye Syndrome, but it is included in the differential due to the presence of pterygium.
The normal serum copper levels make this diagnosis less likely, but it is included in the differential due to the presence of corneal opacities.
There is no evidence to support this diagnosis, but it is included in the differential due to the presence of corneal opacities.
The patient's best spectacle-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 OU despite having 4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma.

rationales.F03: Normal lipid and glucose levels reduce the likelihood of metabolic disorders such as Wilson's Disease and Iron Overload.
rationales.F04: Normal visual acuity reduces the likelihood of severe ocular conditions.
rationales.F06: The presence of corneal ring opacities is a strong indicator of Corneal Opacity and Corneal Ring Opacity.
rationales.F12: Normal serum copper levels rule out Wilson's Disease.
